hero.title: The tool that keeps the plan up to date for you.
hero.subtitle: Ajour is an open source project tool for small projects with 2 to 10 people. You describe the project in plain words, the AI proposes the plan, writes the week's status and suggests changes when reality moves. You decide.

values.aiTitle: The AI maintains, the human decides
values.aiBody: The AI gathers what happened, drafts and proposes changes to the plan. It never sends anything out, never deletes anything and commits nobody to anything without your yes. Everything can be undone.
values.dataBody: Everything a workspace owns can be taken out with one click in open formats and deleted again completely. Hosted with EU-owned providers, or in your own environment with a local language model.
values.securityBody: Passkeys and two-step login from the start, workspaces separated all the way down in the database, and every change in a log that cannot be edited.

ai.setupIntro: Ajour works without a model. For real proposals and free-text answers, set one up:
ai.setupOutro: Then start Ajour again. Without a model the rules engine answers and the three flows still work.
ai.fallbackBody: When no model is configured, or the model does not answer, the {engine} engine steps in.
ai.fallbackDetail: It is deterministic: it lays out a plan from templates, computes replans, drafts a status from what actually happened, and understands set phrases in the chat such as “budget: 80,000”, “obstacle: …” and “decision: …”. It does not advise freely. Cut the internet and the project can still be run.
ai.limitsHint: A model call costs money on a hosted installation and minutes on a local one. The numbers are generous for a person and mean for a script.
ai.principleDecides: The AI proposes and carries out, but the human decides. It never sends anything out of the house and never deletes.
ai.principleUndo: A copy of the whole project is taken before every AI change, and each change can be undone from the message that made it.
ai.principleData: What you and your colleagues write goes to the model as data, never as instructions, and the model's output is validated against the project's own ids before anything is written.
ai.principleSovereign: The model can be swapped, including for a local one. Who can see what is listed in docs/subprocessors.md.
ai.testPatience: A local model may have to be read off disk first. That can take up to a minute the first time.

ai.failUnreachable: Nothing is listening at that address. Is Ollama running? Check OLLAMA_BASE_URL.
ai.failConfig: The model is set up wrong. Correct the model name below, or LLM_MODEL in .env.
ai.failGeneric: The call failed. The details are below and in the server log.
ai.failRateLimited: Mistral refused the call as too many (429). The key works, but the account or plan sets the ceiling: on the free Experiment plan this happens often when the model is busy, and a key under a workspace with no active plan gets the same answer. help.title: Help
help.intro: Two things on this page: how the tool works, and how to run a small project. The second is the more important one.

start.title: Start a project
start.body: Click New project. Describe the project in your own words, or pick one of the templates and a plan is ready at once. The planning engine proposes a goal, milestones and tasks, and you correct and approve. Nothing is saved until you say yes to the plan.

plan.title: Keep the plan up to date
plan.body: Everything is maintained on the project page. Click a task's name to open it: owner, participants, checklist and which milestone it belongs to. Above the task list there is one button per milestone, so you can see only the tasks that carry the one milestone you are working on, and a task added while a filter is on lands under that milestone. Set a task in progress on a day other than its start date and Ajour asks whether to move the date to today. Click a milestone, in the list or on the timeline, to give it an owner, a date and an acceptance criterion. Drag a task on the timeline to move it, up or down to change milestone, at the right edge to change its length; the arrow keys do the same. Drag a milestone and Ajour works out a replan for you to approve or undo.

breakdown.title: Break a milestone into tasks
breakdown.body: A milestone with no tasks under it is a promise with nothing behind it. Click Suggest tasks next to the milestone and the planning engine breaks it into three to seven tasks, dated inside the milestone's window, with a guess at who owns them. You edit, drop and tick, and only when you press create do they become real tasks. A copy of the plan is taken first, so the whole set can be taken back from the history. When you create a new milestone the suggestion is on by default.

tip.title: The daily tip
tip.body: At the top of the project page is the daily tip: the AI has read the whole project and points at the one thing worth doing today. If the tip can be carried out in the plan, the exact instruction Run will send to the AI stands under the tip, so you know what you are saying yes to. Look again asks for a fresh assessment, and Hide puts it away until tomorrow.

economy.title: Budget and spend
economy.body: Set a budget and write the lines in. Each line has an amount it is expected to cost and a number for what has been paid so far, so an instalment or a deposit can be booked without closing the line. Click the row under the line to change what is paid, with All spent and Nothing yet as shortcuts. The bar at the top shows registered and paid in separate colours, so you can see whether the money is running ahead of the work. Money is never shown on the public share link.

status.title: The weekly status
status.body: Click New weekly status. The planning engine reads the plan, assesses it and writes the draft, and the report stands finished beside the fields and updates as you type. The assessment is green, yellow or red, derived from delays, obstacles and spend; you can change it, and the report then says both what the engine proposed and what you chose. Under What management is asked to do you write the decisions or resources only management can provide, with a deadline; items left unanswered carry over to next week's status, marked with when they were first raised. Your own comment appears under your name on the front page. If the engine lacks an answer it asks, and pressing Work the answers in writes them into the text as facts instead of leaving them hanging under it. You can download the draft as a PDF before you approve.

share.title: Share with others
share.body: Every approved status can be downloaded as a two-page PDF: a front page with the assessment, what management is asked for, your comment, the money and the part of the plan that carries the next milestones, and an appendix with the whole timeline, every task, the decisions and the money lines. A share link lets the project be read without a login, with the plan, the milestones and the approved statuses, and the PDF can be downloaded from there. Money, obstacles and the management items never appear on the public link. Under Settings → Data you can export the whole workspace as a spreadsheet or JSON, and delete it again. Tick “Participants can answer through the link” and the link becomes an answer channel: whoever opens it picks their name and can mark their own tasks, leave a note and answer the questions in the latest status, without a login. The answers land in the project with a name on them, and the engine writes the next status from them. At approval you can mail the report to a list of recipients kept on the project, and once a week Ajour can remind you of a status that is missing; both need whoever runs the installation to have set up mail.

model.title: The language model
model.body: Ajour works without a language model: a built-in rules engine lays out plans, writes status drafts and understands fixed phrases in the chat, so you can cut the internet and still run the project. With a model the answers get better. The installation sets one up, and under Settings → AI a workspace can choose its own provider, model and key instead, or turn the model off entirely. Press Test the connection and you are told whether it answers, and what is wrong if it does not. The report always says which engine wrote the draft.

help.abcIntro: Ten things that carry most small projects safely home. None of them needs a project management course.

0.title: Start by describing what finished means
0.body: Not what you are going to do, but what has to be true when the project is over. “The conference was held with 100 people signed up” is a goal. “We are working on the conference” is not. Everything else in the plan hangs off that sentence.

1.title: One owner per task
1.body: Others may help, but one person has the task. Everyone's responsibility is nobody's, and that is the most common reason small projects leak. If you are unsure who it is, it is you.

2.title: Cut the work into pieces of at most a week
2.body: A six-week task cannot be seen slipping. A five-day one can. Small pieces make progress visible and give you something to celebrate every week.

3.title: Milestones are promises, so have few of them
3.body: A milestone is something the outside world can count on. Three to five is enough in a small project. If you cannot explain why a milestone exists, delete it.

4.title: The plan has to tell the truth
4.body: A plan is a picture of reality, not a contract. When reality moves, move the plan, today rather than Friday. An honest plan that slips is worth more than a handsome plan that lies.

5.title: Three questions drive the whole thing
5.body: What has happened? What is next? What is in the way? Answer those three every week and you are, in practice, a project manager. The weekly status here is built on exactly those three questions.

6.title: Bring obstacles into the light at once
6.body: An obstacle rarely gets smaller by waiting. Write it on the list the day you see it, put a name on who is chasing it, and say it out loud in the next status. Nobody blames a project manager for an obstacle, only for hiding one.

7.title: Write decisions down
7.body: In three months nobody will remember why you chose Saturday over Thursday. Two lines in the decision log save you from having the same argument twice.

8.title: Record the money when you know something, not when it is certain
8.body: An estimate of 30,000 today is worth more than an exact figure in a month. Write the line in as planned and change it to incurred when the money is spent. Then the budget never lies to you.

9.title: The status is a gift to yourself
9.body: The weekly status feels like a chore, but it is your pause for thought: five minutes seeing the project from outside. Let the AI write the draft and spend your energy fixing what is wrong. That is where you catch the slip in time.

help.closing: If you are stuck, ask the AI on the project page. It knows your plan and answers from it, and if you ask for changes it makes them at once, in the money, the obstacles and the decisions too. A copy of the plan is always taken first, so everything can be undone from the message that did it.

terms.title: Terms and privacy
terms.intro: Ajour is open source and run by Vinther Consulting at ajour.haij.dk. This page says what you can count on and what we do with what you write. It is short, because the seven dogmas answer most of it: your data is yours, all of it can be exported, and all of it can be deleted.

what.title: What Ajour is
what.body: A tool for keeping small projects up to date: a plan, a weekly status, decisions and obstacles. The code is AGPL-3.0 and public, so you can run exactly this version on your own server if you would rather.

account.title: Accounts and access
account.body: You get in by applying or being invited. We store your name, your email and your workspace's name, and use them to sign you in and to write to you about the service. Passwords are stored hashed, and you can add a passkey and two-factor. We sell nothing, and we do not send marketing you did not ask for.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.body: Everything you write in a workspace is yours. It lives in one database on EU soil with EU-owned providers, separated from other workspaces at the database level. You can take a complete copy as a spreadsheet or JSON at any time under Settings, and delete the whole workspace in the same place. Deleting it also removes the audit trail about it; only the bare fact that a workspace was deleted, by whom and when, remains.

ai.title: The AI
ai.body: The AI proposes and carries out changes to your plan, but it does not decide: a copy of the project is taken before every change, and you can undo all of it. It never sends anything out of the house and never deletes. If the installation uses a hosted model, the project's content is sent to it when you use the chat, the daily tip or the weekly status: the names of the people on the tasks, the milestones, the tasks, the obstacles, the decisions and the budget with its lines. Passwords, passkeys, the audit trail and other workspaces are never sent. The text goes as data, not as instructions. Which model it is is listed in docs/subprocessors.md; if the installation runs locally through Ollama, the text never leaves the server. Under Settings → AI a workspace can choose a different model than the installation uses, or turn the model off entirely. If the workspace chooses its own, that is the provider receiving the text, and the page says which one. An API key a workspace stores is encrypted and cannot be read back out.

shareLinks.title: Share links
shareLinks.body: A share link opens one project's status page for anyone holding it, with no login. It shows the plan, the milestones, the tasks and the approved statuses. It never shows money, obstacles, drafts or the AI chat. You can revoke a link and give it an expiry, and you should do both if the link has been somewhere you did not intend.

leaving.title: Leaving
leaving.body: You can delete your workspace immediately, without writing to anyone and without waiting. The export is one click away and readable without Ajour. We keep no copy afterwards beyond the nightly encrypted backups, which roll off after 30 days.

availability.title: Running and guarantees
availability.body: Ajour is new, and there is no uptime guarantee. We look after your data with encrypted backups every night, but take an export now and then if the project matters. The service is provided as it is, without warranties beyond what the law requires.

license.title: Licence
license.body: The code is AGPL-3.0. You may use it, change it and run it yourself; if you change it and offer it to others over a network, your changes must be available too. What you write in the tool is not covered by the licence — that is yours.

demo.title: The demo
demo.body: Opening a demo makes you a temporary workspace and a temporary account. We do not ask for an email. Both are deleted automatically after {hours} hours, along with everything you wrote in it. Do not put real personal data in a demo.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Write to martin@vintherconsulting.dk. If you have found a security problem, SECURITY.md in the repository says how to report it; use that rather than an ordinary email.
